title: The Rewind: It Is What It Is
summary:
And this is something that I got into more in my memos on risk. But when everybody concludes that something is the
silver bullet, that is the solution that can't fail and has no risk, then
they pile into it, which gives it risk and often leaves it open to failure. The investor, the non-realistic investor, always dreams of finding the silver bullet,
always dreams of finding that investment that will make him a lot of money, but not put him
at risk.

reader_summary.overview: Today, we're featuring another episode of The Rewind, in which Howard looks back on some of his memos over the years, discusses their origins. Today, Howard reflects on It Is What It Is, which was originally published on March 27, 2006. I think it is what it is, is now heard all the time.

thesis: Howard Marks argues that because the future is inherently uncertain and shaped by collective forces beyond individual control, investors must build flexible portfolios that accommodate various environments rather than relying on macro forecasts or attempting to predict specific outcomes. He emphasizes that while one can assess probabilities based on current conditions, actual results will always involve randomness and emotion, meaning investors must accept that even a highly probable outcome can fail, much like drawing a white ball from a bag containing mostly black ones.
